claims.text: The starting CoCrFeNi alloy has an inherently coarse microstructure.
Untreated CoCrFeNi exhibits relatively high friction and wear during sliding.
Laser surface remelting under a controlled atmosphere will produce a nanohierarchical, functionally graded, glaze-like layer on CoCrFeNi.
Real-time microstructure monitoring and laser-parameter adjustment will ensure uniform and stable formation of the adaptive surface layer.
The remelted surface layer will contain adaptive nanoprecipitates and a dense nanocrystalline glaze that evolves with sliding and temperature.
Rapid solidification from laser remelting will generate composition undulations and adaptive nanoprecipitates in CoCrFeNi.
At lower temperatures, the nanohierarchical structure will provide multiple deformation pathways that progressively dissipate frictional stresses.
At elevated temperatures, the adaptive surface structure will reorganize into a dense nanocrystalline glaze layer.
The dense glaze layer will reduce adhesive contact and oxidative wear.
Laser-treated CoCrFeNi will have a significantly lower coefficient of friction than untreated CoCrFeNi from room temperature to 800 °C.
Laser-treated CoCrFeNi will have a significantly lower wear rate than untreated CoCrFeNi from room temperature to 800 °C.
The adaptive surface layer will mitigate tribological degradation under variable loads and environmental conditions.
Untreated CoCrFeNi lacks the adaptive protective surface layer needed to maintain wide-temperature tribological performance.
Loss of surface-layer integrity during extreme thermal cycling or exposure to highly reactive environments may limit the intervention's effectiveness.
The proposed performance scope is limited to sliding from room temperature to 800 °C and standard mechanical loads.
Prior analogous complex-concentrated-alloy systems support the proposed adaptive deformation and high-temperature glaze mechanisms.
The quantitative friction and wear improvements and long-term stability of the modified CoCrFeNi surface remain unvalidated.

contradictions.description: The conditions call for varied environmental conditions, whereas the proposed controlled experiment uses a single fixed controlled atmosphere, so it cannot test the stated environmental breadth.
